messages:
Zoe: quick sync from today's mini-arch huddle. we need to settle where the query router performs permission evaluation vs where it defers to projection for fine-grained checks. also have to account for cost attribution (who gets charged for wasted projection work).
Ravi: tl;dr: router should do cheap checks (tenant identity, API entitlement, route-level deny) and then decide whether to fast-path to cache or to materializer. deep row/column filters stay in projection. avoids pushing schema to router.
Chen: agree on cheap checks. also worried about chargeback: if router forwards unauthenticated/unauthorized stuff and projection does work then billing attribution gets messy. we should define a clear metric: billed_compute_owner = first service that decoded the request body and executed compute.
Priya: proposal: router emits 'compute_owner' tag in the admission token -> projection uses that for billing logs. if router determined it was authorized and forwarded, owner=router; if projection rejects later, owner=projection and we refund/correct billing via backfill.
Alex: refund path is painful. prefer router to be conservative: if it can't confidently authorize cheaply, it should classify request as "needs projection auth" and set compute_owner=projection. only when router can prove coarse-scope allow do we set owner=router.
Zoe: yes. concrete gateway checks: tenant_id, session_valid, route_entitlement, dataset_existence, simple column allowlist. anything beyond that -> needs projection auth.
Ravi: caching semantics: router classifies responses as cacheable_public, cacheable_tenant, or non-cacheable. projection honors that classification but must still attach provenance headers.
Chen: suggestion: include a cache_vsig (versioned signature) in token so projection can validate cache-class wasn't downgraded by router. avoids downgrade attack where a router marks response as public incorrectly.
Priya: token structure example (compact):

[tid|sid|scope_hash|exp|cache_class|vsig].hmac

where cache_class in {public, tenant, private} and vsig = short version id for projection schema.

Alex: also add telemetry fields: router emits route_latency estimate and request_size hint. projection logs actual compute and we reconcile in analytics pipeline to compute wasted work ratio.
Zoe: perf targets: router auth path must be <1ms p50, projection auth <0.5ms additional. add bench for 99th percentile under 2k rps.
Ravi: rollout plan: feature-flag hybrid-auth in three phases:
1) Observe-only: router sets classification, projection enforces always. logs only. 2) Soft-enforce: router returns 403 for obvious denies (global blacklists) but otherwise sets compute_owner=projection. 3) Enforce: router sets compute_owner and denies requests it can cheaply reject.
Chen: add a metric: "auth_mismatch_rate" when router says allowed but projection rejects; aim for <0.1% before moving phases.
Priya: ops: add a Circuit-Breaker rule: if session-service latency > 200ms, router should fall back to "projection-authorize" mode to avoid blocking and keep tail stable.
Alex: security: deny-by-default on mismatch. if router claims allow but projection rejects, projection should log at high severity and emit a signal to SRE.
Zoe: small example cache-key patterns for docs: 
- public: hash(model||projection||time_bucket||proj_vsig)
- tenant: hash(tenant||model||projection||time_bucket||proj_vsig)
- private: non-cacheable (store ephemeral only)

Ravi: action items:
- Priya: draft compact token spec and HMAC format + vsig semantics (due Wed)
- Chen: implement metric pipeline check for auth_mismatch_rate and wasted_compute_ratio (due Fri)
- Alex: add bench job for p99 router auth under 2k rps (due Thu)
- Zoe: update RFC with phased rollout and circuit-breaker thresholds (due Mon)
- eng-bot: create ticket 'query-router-authz-cache-accounting' and tag assignees (reply when created)
eng-bot: Created ticket INF-7921 with title 'query-router-authz-cache-accounting' and assignees Priya,Chen,Alex,Zoe. due_date:2024-05-10
Chen: one more: include a reconciliation job that periodically reconciles billed_compute_owner vs actual compute logs to correct billing; schedule weekly initially.
Ravi: +1. keep runbook for manual refunds if reconciliation shows >0.05% mismatches for a week.
Zoe: solid. thanks all, i'll circulate the draft and we'll review in next arch sync. :sparkles:
